# Example Statistical Manipulations

Consider the following data, indicating nothing meaningful:

```{r}
# 20 randomly picked numbers within the [0,12] integer interval
dataset <- sample(0:12, 20, replace = TRUE)
```

Now, we can print a summary of all statistics:

```{r}
summary(dataset)
```

Now, let us assume that we are interested in a table of frequencies for the above:

```{r}
table(dataset)
```

Let us also plot a simple barplot:

```{r}
barplot(table(dataset))
```

Also, we can get the relative frequencies relatively easily:

```{r}
pmf <- table(dataset) / 20
print(pmf)
```
Observe, that this also corresponds to the Probability Mass Function (PMF).

We might also be interested into the Cummulative Distribution Function (CDF):

```{r}
cdf <- function(n) {
  s <- 0
  for (i in 1:n) {
    if (pmf[i] < n) {
      s <- s + pmf[i]
    }
  }
}
```
